context.task: Locate and open the overdue task

scope: Initial work-queue composition at two widths and activation of the overdue task only; other controls are mocked.
label: Modern SaaS minimalism preference fit
weightProvenance: User-requested preference; weights and anchors authored for this skill, not empirically validated.

task.reason: Only the scoped overdue-row activation was probed; programmatic focus plus Enter opened the matching task. Discovery by users was not tested.

legibility.reason: Rendered appearance inspected; complete contrast/accessibility checks were not run.
evidence: No complete contrast or accessibility assessment supplied

interaction.reason: Task-row Enter activation and detail focus passed; navigation, toolbar and New task are nonfunctional mock controls, so this is not an approved working app.

adaptation.reason: Two widths have no root overflow; phone hides owner/due/sidebar and long content was not stress-tested. Full information availability remains unverified.

breakdown.label: Quiet hierarchy
breakdown.anchor: Several unrelated elements compete with the main task.
breakdown.reason: The large tinted header and purple sidebar compete with the operational rows.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Reduce header area and sidebar emphasis while preserving orientation.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Restrained surfaces
breakdown.anchor: Heavy shadows, pills or boxes dominate without structural purpose.
breakdown.reason: The framed main panel, framed header and raised row cards repeat containment; every row has a 24px radius.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Remove the outer decorative frame and raised row treatment; retain meaningful list grouping.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Typography-led composition
breakdown.anchor: Mostly compact type roles with distracting size/weight/wrapping drift.
breakdown.reason: 42px desktop heading visually dominates a four-row work queue; row labels remain readable.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Try the same 24px app-heading role as the restrained candidate, retaining body text.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Useful density and rhythm
breakdown.anchor: Useful content fits, but grouping or whitespace remains uneven.
breakdown.reason: Extra row padding and card gaps spread comparable items while all four rows still fit.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Bring related records closer and retain deliberate space between the header and toolbar.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Precise component language
breakdown.anchor: Related control geometry, restrained radii and crisp icons; explicit labels where needed.
breakdown.reason: Rounded controls and pills form a consistent family even though their heavy treatment is not preferred.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Keep consistent controls; tune geometry at the shared token rather than random per-row fixes.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Purposeful color
breakdown.anchor: Saturated containers and competing accents dilute priority.
breakdown.reason: Every status receives the same lavender badge and the Overdue color distinction is lost.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Keep written status labels and reserve color variation for meaningful status or selection.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.

breakdown.label: Product-specific restraint
breakdown.anchor: Coherent but generic treatment with limited connection to product content.
breakdown.reason: The purple frame and card treatment feel generic rather than specific to exception handling.
breakdown.tradeoff: This is reviewer interpretation of one authored queue, not participant preference or a rule for other screen idioms.
breakdown.nextChange: Keep product/task vocabulary and reduce generic showcase treatments.
breakdown.preserve: The four task identities, written statuses and working task-detail activation.
